one_liner: Pure-Go, dependency-free WebAssembly MVP interpreter with an optional arm64/amd64 JIT; beats wazero's interpreter 1.1-1.8x on micro-loops.
what_it_does: Embeds WebAssembly 1.0 (MVP) modules in a Go program without cgo: wasman.NewModule decodes and fully validates, wasman.NewInstance or a Linker instantiates with Go host functions, and Instance.CallExportedFunc runs exports. It adds per-opcode gas metering (TollStation), call-depth and memory caps, context cancellation, Reset for instance pooling and an optional u128/u256 import namespace for EVM-style math. The API is its own, not wazero's Runtime/api.Function shape.
how_it_is_fast: The interpreter pre-decodes each function body at load time into side tables (immediates, branch targets, block lookups), pools call frames, takes loop back-branches directly and dispatches trap-free hot opcodes through an inlined jump table, which brings Fib down to about 1 allocation per exported call against wazero-interp's 21,893. EnableJIT adds a tiered compiler: an optimizing tier with a virtual-register IR, linear-scan register allocation, compare/branch fusion, loop rotation and a native calling convention between compiled functions, and a baseline template tier for the rest (notably float code). Memory accesses keep an explicit address+offset+width check against the memory length (no guard pages).
when_to_use: A Go service that must run small MVP Wasm modules (plugins, rules, smart-contract code) with no cgo and no third-party dependencies in the main module.
Instantiate-heavy workloads such as one fresh instance per request: 2.1 us to decode, validate and instantiate the Fib module on an Apple M3, plus Reset to recycle instances.
Deterministic metered execution: per-opcode TollStation gas with bit-identical trap points between interpreter and baseline JIT, plus u256.mul_div and u256.isqrt imports for DeFi-style arithmetic.
Memory-bound kernels on linux or darwin with arm64/amd64 and EnableJIT, where it led wazero's compiler (MemRW 1.8x, Sort 1.3x on the M3).
Environments that forbid executable memory, where the interpreter mode was 1.1-1.8x faster than wazero's interpreter on the author's loops.
when_not_to_use: Modules built for Wasm 2.0 or later: SIMD, threads, tail calls, exceptions, memory64 and the memory.init, data.drop and table.* bulk-memory ops are not implemented (passive segments are parsed but not applied), and no WASI layer is documented.
Call-heavy or call_indirect-heavy code under the JIT: wazero's compiler was 9% ahead on Fib and 1.4x ahead on Indirect on the M3, and 1.6x ahead on Fib on a dual EPYC 7K62.
When you need to cancel runaway guest code with the JIT on: interrupts are only checked when native code returns to Go at a call site (see gotchas).
Windows, FreeBSD or other OS/architecture pairs where you need native speed: the JIT is built only for (darwin or linux) and (arm64 or amd64); everything else runs the interpreter.
Production use that needs a track record: 11 stars, no issues ever filed, a single maintainer, and the JIT plus several correctness fixes landed in a burst between 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-19.

integration.dependencies: none (the bench/ subdirectory is a separate Go module that pulls in wazero, wagon and life)
integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.18 per go.mod (CI installs '^1.18', which resolves to the latest Go, so 1.18 itself is not exercised); the bench module declares go 1.25.0
integration.platforms: any Go target for the interpreter; JIT only on linux and darwin for arm64 and amd64 (build tags in wasm/jit), with per-function interpreter fallback
integration.thread_safety: An Instance is single-goroutine (source comment: no locking); Interrupt is safe to call from any goroutine; use one instance per goroutine or pool them with Reset.

gotchas: With EnableJIT, Interrupt and CallExportedFuncWithContext are checked only when native code exits to Go at a call site (wasm/jit_native.go). The jit.Ctx ABI has no interrupt field, loop back-edges jump without a poll in both tiers, and the interrupt tests (instance_features_test.go) run the interpreter only. A call-free loop compiled by the JIT therefore probably cannot be cancelled, despite the README's 'interruption rails' claim; use a TollStation, which forces the inline-metered baseline tier.

The '19220/19220, 0 skipped' conformance badge covers the WebAssembly 1.0 MVP suites plus memory_fill and memory_copy (the list in spectest/gen.sh), not the current full testsuite. Its generated testdata is not committed and CI installs no wabt, so CI skips the spec run; the badge is a local result.

The JIT recompiles every function for each NewInstance (compiled code is owned by the instance; no shared compiled-module cache). It is switched off entirely by CanonicalizeNaNs or by a TollStation with non-uniform opcode prices, and any metering drops the optimizing tier, so metered JIT runs at baseline-tier speed.

The benchmark harness is fair on correctness (every timed call checks its result) but its Instantiate row makes wazero create and close a whole Runtime per iteration, which inflates the 6.6x win. The tables are single runs that state Go 1.24 while bench/go.mod now requires Go 1.25. The repo root also carries wasman.test, a 4.7 MB darwin/arm64 Mach-O test binary, which is part of the module source.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (DTVM, KinoWASM, WasmKit, Cage on Wasmtime, VectorVisor) are C++, Rust or Swift engines that a Go program could only reach through cgo or a subprocess; pick wasman when a pure-Go, dependency-free embed matters more than peak speed or Wasm 2.0 coverage.
verified_claims_summary: The author's go test -bench harness (Go 1.24 per the page, Apple M3, single runs, tiny .wat fixtures) measured wasman's interpreter 1.83x faster than wazero v1.12's interpreter on Fib(20), 1.30x on a 100k Sum loop and 1.08x on 64 KiB MemRW, with instantiation 6.6x faster where wazero's row includes Runtime setup and teardown. In JIT mode it beat wazero's compiler on MemRW (1.8x) and Sort (1.3x), tied on Sum and Dispatch, and trailed on Fib (9%), Hash (9%), Mandel (3%) and Indirect (1.4x).
status_note: Active (145 commits, last on 2026-08-19 after a five-day JIT and fix burst) and MIT-licensed pure Go, so copyable, but a one-maintainer project with 11 stars and no outside bug reports; LICENSE also credits @mathetake's gasm, the ancestor of wazero.
